item.title: Yoshino Kuzu: The Translucent Sweet of the Mountains — Guide
item.description: Yoshino kuzu is one of Japan’s most refined traditional ingredients: a pure white starch painstakingly extracted from the roots of wild kudzu vines and refined by hand in cold mountain water, a labour-intensive craft centred on the Yoshino region. Prized for its smooth, glossy texture, real Yoshino hon-kuzu transforms into some of the most elegant wagashi in Japan — silken, jelly-like kuzumochi dusted with kinako and syrup, translucent kuzukiri noodles dipped in kuromitsu, and, in winter, kuzuyu, a warm, soothing thickened drink.
